questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Student environment, and the vibe of the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, all the information I needed was there. The only isse might be that there is so much information that one might have trouble finding the information that applies to one's own situation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance, but I think if one needed it and reached out there would be someone who would help you out. It appeared to me that there was a lot of options and help available if need be.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied for university accommodation. I applied a bit later, because I originally had heard that it was almost impossible to get it via the university. So always give it a try, even if you apply a few weeks or a month after others.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was really nice living away from campus because I felt like I got to see more of the city and not just campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was really nice. My only issue was that it was really dirty when I first arrived, but after cleaning it myself it was a nice place and it had all of the facilities I needed. One thing students should now is that most places will not have anything, so the kitchens will be almost empty, there will be the basics, like and oven, but no plates, knives, pots and pans. Ask the reception, there might be stuff that previous students left behind.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is a process that you go through for over 6 months, you receive all of the help and information you need, but you do have to continuously read emails, fill out forms, apply for things and such.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the host institution and then they would help you get into contact with the specific office and people that could help out with whatever issue or concerns you had.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went fairly easy and I got into all of the classes I applied for as my first choice. There was one class that I had originally wanted that did not become available to visiting students, but they had a lot of other interesting options.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I had tried to get an overview of classes, and sort of decided which ones I wanted before class registration opened up, so that I was prepared to send in the applications for classes on the same day that it opened up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took third year courses. At the university they have four years on their BA, however those courses did not seem to be available to me. It is difficult to get into higher level courses, like third year courses, on stuff that you are not directly registered to be studying. For example my education in Copenhagen is broader and includes some different fields, but I could not get into higher level courses on those other subjects, only one overall, which is one of the main focuses of my education. However, I could of course have taken first year courses in other subjects.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Classes were a bit more of a group discussion, not as much 'teaching'.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Creative Writing Part 2: Prose
Ideology and Literature
George Orwell and the Politics of Literature

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Creative Writing Part 2: Prose 
It was a really good experience, a really good teacher who created a good and safe learning environment.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Costs for kitchen stuff. I spend probably over a 1000 DKK on cutlery and kitchen stuff.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Vegestables and fruit is a little bit expensive. Unhealthy food can be quite cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of options, something for everyone.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything, there were so many student societies (clubs), of all kinds.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on trips, and experience the country and nature, it is incredibly beautiful, and I am so happy that I not only got to see the host city, but also the country.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go explore, sign up for student societies, travel.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy. Pretty similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The teachers are not as open to different interpretations, there is a bit more a culture of right and wrong answers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and peoples willingness to help out.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Seek out other people and societies early on. 
Read some of the texts in advance, you will want to do other stuff than just sit and read and study all of the time when you are on exchange. 
Go see the nature and the highland, it is so remarkable and beautiful. Buy hiking boots, very important, they are worth every penny.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Save up money to that it won't be a problem when you arrive. I was so happy that I did not have to worry about what I could afford.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a different culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: How to prioritise your time between meeting people, experiencing new things, studies and visitors from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
